Let <MATH_0001> be a property of morphisms of algebraic spaces
which is <ACCENT_0001>tale-smooth local on the source-and-target.
We say a DM morphism <MATH_0002> of algebraic stacks
<TEXTITOPEN_0001>has property <MATH_0003><TEXTITCLOSE_0001> if the equivalent conditions of
Lemma <REF_0001>
hold.

Let <MATH_0001> be a property of morphisms of algebraic spaces
which is <ACCENT_0001>tale-smooth local on the source-and-target and
stable under composition. Then the property of DM morphisms of algebraic stacks
defined in Definition <REF_0001>
is stable under composition. Namely, let <MATH_0002>
and <MATH_0003> be DM morphisms of algebraic stacks
having property <MATH_0004>. By Lemma <REF_0002>
the composition <MATH_0005> is DM. Choose an algebraic space <MATH_0006> and a
surjective smooth morphism <MATH_0007>. Choose an algebraic space
<MATH_0008> and a surjective <ACCENT_0002>tale morphism <MATH_0009>
(Lemma <REF_0003>).
Choose an algebraic space <MATH_0010> and a surjective <ACCENT_0003>tale morphism
<MATH_0011>. Then the morphisms
<MATH_0012> and <MATH_0013> have property <MATH_0014> by definition.
Whence <MATH_0015> has property <MATH_0016> as we assumed that
<MATH_0017> is stable under composition. Thus, by definition again,
we see that <MATH_0018> has
property <MATH_0019>.

Let <MATH_0001> be a property of morphisms of algebraic spaces
which is <ACCENT_0001>tale-smooth local on the source-and-target and
stable under base change. Then the property of
DM morphisms of algebraic stacks defined in
Definition <REF_0001>
is stable under arbitrary base change.
Namely, let <MATH_0002>
be a DM morphism of algebraic stacks
and <MATH_0003> be a morphism of algebraic stacks
and assume <MATH_0004> has property <MATH_0005>.
Then the base change
<MATH_0006>
is a DM morphism by Lemma <REF_0002>.
Choose an algebraic space <MATH_0007>
and a surjective smooth morphism <MATH_0008>. Choose an algebraic
space <MATH_0009> and a surjective <ACCENT_0002>tale morphism
<MATH_0010> (Lemma <REF_0003>).
Finally, choose an algebraic space
<MATH_0011> and a surjective and smooth morphism
<MATH_0012>. Then the morphism
<MATH_0013> has property <MATH_0014> by definition.
Whence <MATH_0015> has property <MATH_0016> as we assumed that
<MATH_0017> is stable under base change. Considering the diagram
<MATH_0018>
we see that the left top horizontal arrow is surjective and
<MATH_0019>
is <ACCENT_0003>tale as a base change of <MATH_0020>,
whence by definition we see that the projection
<MATH_0021> has
property <MATH_0022>.
